answer: Fork-Priced Identity Ledger.** Each new identity must submit a distinct dependency graph of prior actions; the protocol computes a similarity score against every existing node and charges registration in proportion to graph overlap, so clones land near a shared summit of cost while genuinely new agents pay little. Every duplicate pair also increments a public mirror counter, raising the price for the next entrant in that cluster. A garden of unrelated agents therefore stays cheap, while a sybil cluster's total registration cost grows with its squared size,
